title: 4.5. Dictionaries: Key-Value Mapping & Structured Data
summary: Work with Python dictionaries (dict): unordered/insertion-ordered key-value mappings. Master keys(), values(), items(), get(), and in membership testing.
learningObjectives: Construct dictionaries using curly braces {key: value}.
Recognize key requirements: dictionary keys must be immutable types (strings, numbers, tuples).

sections.heading: 4.5.1 Dictionaries as Key-Value Stores
sections.content:
A dictionary is an associative data structure where each value is accessed via a unique key rather than an integer index.

• Keys: Must be immutable (strings, integers, floats, booleans, tuples). Keys must be unique.
• Values: Can be of any arbitrary data type (lists, numbers, other dictionaries).
• Safe Lookup: user_dict.get('email', 'default@example.com') retrieves values without raising KeyError.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which of the following CANNOT be used as a dictionary key in Python?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Dictionary keys must be immutable and hashable. Lists are mutable, so they cannot serve as dictionary keys.

recap: Dictionaries provide O(1) key-value access; keys must be immutable, values can be any type.
